question: Around which postnatal days do maternity blues most commonly show up?
explanation: Maternity blues typically peak within the first week after birth, most commonly between days three and five as hormone levels shift rapidly. [learn more](BMP223_U2_T1#BMP223_U2_T1_h1)

question: Why might cultural expectations in Nigeria make coping with baby blues tough for a new mother?

options.A: Pressure to constantly display joy can mask her distress
options.B: Extended families usually refuse to visit new mothers
options.C: Community members generally ignore postpartum women
options.D: Traditions forbid her from breastfeeding in public

explanation: Societal norms often expect a woman to be purely joyous after delivery, which can make her feel guilty or isolated when she experiences unexpected sadness. [learn more](BMP223_U2_T1#BMP223_U2_T1_h1)

question: Which specific hormones drop sharply right after childbirth?
explanation: The sudden withdrawal of high pregnancy levels of estrogen and progesterone triggers the emotional volatility seen in baby blues. [learn more](BMP223_U2_T1#BMP223_U2_T1_h2)

question: A first-time mum who had an emergency caesarean section complains of tiredness and sudden crying spells on day four. What is the main cause?

options.A: An early sign of irreversible postpartum psychosis
options.B: Combined physiological hormone withdrawal and surgical pain
options.C: A chronic nutritional deficiency developed during pregnancy
options.D: Total rejection of the newborn infant by the mother

explanation: Surgical recovery, sleep loss, and hormonal shifts combine to create the classic picture of early postpartum mood lability. [learn more](BMP223_U2_T1#BMP223_U2_T1_h2)

question: Which of the following is NOT a feature of normal maternity blues?
explanation: Suicidal thoughts are never a feature of baby blues; their presence indicates a severe depressive disorder requiring urgent intervention. [learn more](BMP223_U2_T1#BMP223_U2_T1_h3)

question: How do mood swings typically show up in a woman experiencing maternity blues?

options.A: She remains permanently sad and completely unresponsive
options.B: She shows total apathy and refuses to hold her baby
options.C: She shifts rapidly between happiness and sudden crying
options.D: She displays unprovoked anger toward every visitor

explanation: Lability means the mood is changeable; mothers often laugh one minute and cry the next over minor matters. [learn more](BMP223_U2_T1#BMP223_U2_T1_h3)

question: What is the main difference in timing that helps a midwife separate baby blues from postpartum depression?

options.A: Baby blues last for several months without getting better
options.B: Baby blues only happen at night, while depression occurs all day
options.C: Baby blues resolve within two weeks, whereas depression persists longer
options.D: Depression starts on day one, while blues start at six weeks

explanation: Duration is a key diagnostic marker; symptoms lasting past the first fortnight point away from simple blues and toward depression. [learn more](BMP223_U2_T1#BMP223_U2_T1_h4)

question: Which condition allows the mother to maintain her daily routines and care for her baby without major problems?
explanation: Maternity blues are self-limiting and mild, allowing the mother to continue functioning, unlike depressive disorders which impair daily life. [learn more](BMP223_U2_T1#BMP223_U2_T1_h4)

question: Why is simple reassurance from the midwife so powerful for a woman experiencing baby blues?

options.A: It relieves her fear that she is losing her mind
options.B: It forces her to stop crying within a few minutes
options.C: It immediately cures the underlying hormonal imbalance
options.D: It replaces the need for any family support system

explanation: Many women fear their sudden sadness means they are mentally unstable; knowing it is a common, temporary phase brings immense relief. [learn more](BMP223_U2_T1#BMP223_U2_T1_h5)

question: What is the main care plan for uncomplicated maternity blues?

options.A: Admission to a psychiatric ward for observation
options.B: Immediate prescription of heavy antidepressant drugs
options.D: Complete separation of mother and infant for rest

explanation: Because baby blues are self-limiting, medical treatment is unnecessary; emotional support and reassurance are the standard care. [learn more](BMP223_U2_T1#BMP223_U2_T1_h5)

question: How can educating the husband and family members help a mother with baby blues?

options.A: They can isolate her from visitors to prevent emotional stress
options.B: They can provide practical help and avoid making harsh judgments
options.C: They can take over total custody of the newborn baby
options.D: They can prescribe local herbal remedies to balance hormones

explanation: Involving family ensures the mother receives practical burden-sharing and emotional empathy rather than criticism. [learn more](BMP223_U2_T1#BMP223_U2_T1_h6)

question: A mother-in-law complains at the postnatal clinic that the new mother is just lazy and crying for nothing. What should the midwife do?

options.A: Scold the mother-in-law for lacking traditional wisdom
options.B: Immediately refer the mother to a psychiatric hospital
options.C: Explain kindly that temporary mood swings are normal after birth
options.D: Advise the family to send the mother back to her parents

explanation: Educating the family corrects misconceptions and turns potential critics into supportive caregivers. [learn more](BMP223_U2_T1#BMP223_U2_T1_h6)

question: Which symptom makes a psychiatric referral essential for a postnatal woman?

options.A: Thoughts of harming herself or her baby
options.B: Mild fatigue due to waking up for feeds
options.D: Occasional crying spells in the evening

explanation: Any form of self-harm ideation or thoughts of harming the infant are psychiatric emergencies requiring specialist care. [learn more](BMP223_U2_T1#BMP223_U2_T1_h7)

question: At what point should a midwife stop treating a mood change as simple baby blues and suspect depression?

options.A: When the mother cries on the second day
options.B: When family members visit the clinic
options.C: When symptoms last longer than two weeks
options.D: When the baby wakes up twice at night

explanation: The two-week threshold is the clinical dividing line separating temporary blues from developing depression. [learn more](BMP223_U2_T1#BMP223_U2_T1_h7)
